messages:
Ashley: Heads-up: planning a Terraform change to add a traceflow-friendly canary NAT + ephemeral EIP for GPU subnets. Need a quick sanity check before we apply in staging.

Ben: sgtm. can you paste the TF diff? also which NAT will this use (existing vs new)?

Ashley: quick diff snippet: ```resource "aws_route" "egress_to_nat_canary" {
  route_table_id       = aws_route_table.egress.id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  nat_gateway_id       = aws_nat_gateway.canary.id
}
``` using a new natgw in az-b with an ephemeral EIP allocated by TF and tagged for canary.

Lia: small concern: routing precedence with TGW attachments. If we add an explicit 0.0.0.0/0 route to the subnet RT it might interact with TGW propagated routes. need to confirm propagate flags and assoc ordering.

Ben: TF plan looks like the same destination will be added to the subnet's route table that currently has a TGW route (propagated). AWS chooses explicit over propagated, but propagation timing can be funky. @Lia want me to run a dry-run apply in staging?

Lia: please run plan+apply in staging, then run an aws CLI check: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids <id>` and also do a traceflow from a pod. we added a traceflow daemonset in kube a few weeks ago.

Ashley: running plan in staging now. traceflow command we use: ```kubectl exec -n nettest pod/trace-pod -- /usr/local/bin/traceflow --dst 8.8.8.8 --proto TCP``` will show the path by ENI. will paste output after apply.

devops-bot: terraform plan for infra/nat-canary (staging) queued by Ben — check https://ci.redwood/plan/3298 :eyes: :gear:

Ashley: plan applied in staging (no prod changes). traceflow output (5 runs):
- run1: src ENI eni-0abc -> nat-0f12 -> igw-06d
- run2: src ENI eni-0abc -> tgw-attach-xyz -> tgw -> igw (unexpected)
- run3: src ENI eni-0abc -> nat-0f12 -> igw-06d
- run4: src ENI eni-0abc -> nat-0f12 -> igw-06d
- run5: src ENI eni-0abc -> tgw-attach-xyz -> tgw

Two of five packets took the TGW path. seems like propagation / route convergence issue.

Ben: sounds like async propagation from TGW is the culprit. explicit vs propagated routes race on some hosts. In AWS you can't set route priority; we should isolate the canary into its own subnet + RT so we don't conflict with TGW routes.

Lia: +1 to a separate canary subnet. also make sure the ephemeral EIP allocation doesn't get sucked into our shared EIP pool automation. add tags `redwood:canary=true` and `owner:infra-canary`. set `propagate=false` on TGW attachment for that AZ/subnet.

Ashley: will rework TF plan: create aws_subnet.canary, aws_eip.nat_canary (with lifecycle create_before_destroy), aws_nat_gateway.canary, aws_route_table.canary + aws_route_table_association. will add tags and policy. pinging oncall @Maria for final signoff.

Maria: oncall quick look — canary subnet approach looks good. two asks before approve: 1) ensure TGW attachment has `auto_accept`/propagate=false for this attachment to avoid accidental propagation; 2) add k8s scheduling hints (nodeSelector/affinity) so traceflow pods land in same AZ as the canary NAT. :thumbsup:

Ashley: perfect. I'll open PR with plan output + small diagram and request reviews from Ben/Lia/Maria. ETA EOD today.
